newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks end up on talk of imminent govt steps.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks end up on talk of imminent govt steps.

text.p: Shares closed higher on Wednesday after fluctuating widely, and brokers said sharp rises towards the close were based on talk that the government would soon announce specific market boosting measures.
The composite stock index provisionally ended the session 10.36 points higher at 621.41. It touched the psychologically sensitive support level of 600 before rebounding.
But declining shares continued to outnumber advancers, 491 to 330.

"The market rose in late trading due to rumours that there will be an announcement this afternoon," said broker Choe Seung-wook of Schroders Securities. "But I think investors are clutching at straws."
In afternoon trading, the market sank to a low of 600.56, hit by selling, primarily in smaller-cap shares, to meet margin loan calls.
"Share prices have dropped so much that loans for margin trading are being called. This is putting more downward pressure on the market," said a Seoul Securities broker.
The market was dampened by rumours -- denied by the company -- that Hanbo Steel was facing bankruptcy. Hanbo shares closed down 420 won to their lower limit of 4,880.

Finance ministry officials said earlier that the government was considering increasing boosting measures, including raising the capital of the Korea Fund, an offshore fund specialising in South Korean equities, in the first quarter.

Financial shares led after President Kim Young-sam emphasised the need for financial reform during Tuesday's news conference. SEOULBANK rose 320 won to its limit of 4,420 and Commercial Bank of Korea gained 420 won to 5,720.
